chunks: And Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Going out on the day of al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā to the open prayer area is good for whoever is able to go out to it."
He said: So I said, "What do you think if he is sick and is not able to go out—should he pray in his house?" He said: "No."

key_terms.الْجَبَّانَةِ: the open area outside the town used for prayer

ai.seo_question: Should a sick person who cannot go out perform the Eid prayer at home?
ai.summary: This hadith states that going out to the open area for the Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer is good for the one who is able. It also indicates that if a sick person cannot go out, he should not perform that Eid prayer in his house. The narration relates to the fiqh of the two Eid prayers and their proper setting.
